answer: Run every claimed piece of work three times, on three different machines, and pay only when all three runs produce the same result. A sybil farmer cannot reuse one fake computation across clones because each identity's work is re-executed independently, so a hundred clones cost a hundred times the compute of one honest agent, and the fraud shows up the moment any run diverges. Like a trellis that keeps every vine apart, the three runs keep every claim separate, and an ember of fake work that glows once is exposed when the next run finds nothing but a raven picking through cold ash.
